primary_sources.title: Local Clique Covering of Graphs

locators.support: Boolean rank is the minimum number of all-one submatrices covering all one entries; for a bipartite adjacency matrix those rectangles correspond to bicliques and give r_B(A)=bc(G).
Local Boolean rank bounds the number of selected rectangles containing each row or column, and the source states lr_B(A)=lbc(G).

primary_sources.source_limit: The paper does not separately state the empty-support normalization used by this proposal.

primary_sources.title: Non-deterministic Communication Complexity with Few Witnesses

locators.support: The source defines unrestricted rectangle-cover number κ(M), entry degree, and κ_k(M), where k bounds per-cell cover multiplicity.
The source defines nondeterministic protocol complexity n(f) as maximum leaf depth and n_k(f) by witness multiplicity at most k.
For nonempty 1-support, the stated formula is n(f)=ceil(log2 κ(M_f)); the proof names t cover rectangles using ceil(log2 t) bits.

source_limits: The printed proposition says any function but does not resolve κ(M_f)=0: log2(0) is undefined and the proof assumes a cover of size t that can be encoded.
The source notation n_1(f) denotes witness multiplicity at most one and is not the superscript N^1 notation proposed for the accepting side.

The local downloaded byte copy required disabled TLS certificate verification after verified clients rejected the host chain; semantic verification therefore rests on direct reading of the same official primary URL, while the local hash is acquisition metadata only.

primary_sources.title: Contentment in graph theory: Covering graphs with cliques
primary_sources.author: James B. Orlin
primary_sources.support: Historical provenance that biclique edge covering has a natural matrix translation.
primary_sources.source_limit: No full article was reviewed; this source cannot carry any exact equality or edge-case claim in the map.

conditions: X and Y are finite and nonempty.
rc_1 covers the 1-support with arbitrary overlap and no zero cells.
relationship_decisions.proof_check: Each factor column/row pair has rectangular support and Boolean OR takes the union; conversely each rectangle supplies indicator vectors for one factor.
relationship_decisions.zero_case: With empty disjunction equal to 0 and the empty rectangle family admissible, both values are 0. This is a project definition and proof, not a separately stated S1 edge case.

conditions: Its labeled bipartition X disjoint-union Y is fixed, with X and Y nonempty.
Only edge-bearing bicliques matter; their sides align with X and Y.
relationship_decisions.proof_check: The edge set of a biclique with sides S subseteq X and T subseteq Y is exactly the all-one rectangle S x T, preserving cover cardinality in both directions.
relationship_decisions.zero_case: For an edgeless graph on the fixed nonempty sides, the equality uses the project convention that the empty biclique and rectangle families are covers of size 0.

relationship_decisions.supported_core: For nonzero f, after identifying atlas N^1 with S2 n(f) and atlas rc_1 with S2 unrestricted κ, S2 Proposition 3 gives the claimed formula.
required_convention_mapping: Atlas superscript N^1 means acceptance on the 1-side and equals S2 n(f).
Atlas rc_1 means covering 1-cells and equals S2 κ(M); it is not S2 κ_1(M).
S2 subscript n_1(f) means witness multiplicity at most one and corresponds to κ_1, not to atlas N^1.
relationship_decisions.zero_case: For all-zero f, define rc_1(M_f)=0 by the empty cover and define N^1(f)=0 via a depth-zero constant-reject protocol. The max(1,.) formula then follows as a local totalization; do not attribute that resolution to the printed proposition.
relationship_decisions.complement_case: N^0(f):=N^1(1-f) is an atlas definition of the rejecting side; S2 uses n(complement f), not this superscript notation.

conditions: The fixed bipartition and labels are retained.
The objective counts selected rectangles containing each row or column and selected bicliques containing each corresponding vertex.
It does not count how many rectangles cover an individual cell.
relationship_decisions.proof_check: The rectangle-biclique correspondence is objectwise and preserves membership of every row/column index as membership of the corresponding vertex, so it preserves the maximum incidence objective.
relationship_decisions.zero_case: The empty cover gives incidence 0 on every vertex/row/column when X,Y are nonempty; this normalization should be labeled local.

guardrail_decisions.note: S2 Proposition 2 uses an ordinary sum only for κ_1, whose per-cell degree at most one makes the nonzero rectangles disjoint. It does not convert arbitrary overlapping Boolean covers into ordinary-rank decompositions.
S1 local incidence is per row/column or graph vertex; S2 k-cover degree is per matrix cell/input.
S2 explicitly separates deterministic c(f) from nondeterministic n(f) and says no analogous exact deterministic characterization is known.
Each cross-domain edge must retain its typed translation and assumptions.

required_changes.change: Replace the dimension sentence with: Let X and Y be finite nonempty sets throughout. Empty support means the all-zero matrix on X x Y; it does not mean an empty index set.
State that rc_1 means rectangle cover of the 1-support and maps to S2 κ(M), while S2 κ_1(M) is the distinct multiplicity-one cover/partition parameter.
Define atlas N^1 as S2 n(f) under the cited max-leaf-depth protocol convention, and warn that superscript N^1 is not S2 subscript n_1(f).
Label every zero-support value as an adopted empty-family/empty-disjunction convention with a short local proof; do not imply S1 or S2 explicitly states all of those edge cases.

For the converse in R3, describe S2’s convention precisely: the first party nondeterministically names a cover rectangle compatible with its row and the second party tests its column. Avoid presenting the equality as convention-independent certificate complexity.
Present N^0(f):=N^1(1-f) as the atlas rejecting-side definition and show the mapping to S2 n(complement f), rather than attributing the superscript notation to S2.

recommended_map_wording.scope: Let X and Y be finite nonempty sets. Empty support means A is all-zero on X x Y. We allow k=0, use empty OR = 0, and allow the empty cover family.
recommended_map_wording.rectangle_notation: rc_1(A) denotes an unrestricted cover of the 1-support by all-one rectangles; the subscript names the cell value being covered. It corresponds to κ(A) in Karchmer et al., not their κ_1(A).
recommended_map_wording.communication_concept: Write N^1_S2(f) for Karchmer et al.’s n(f), the minimum maximum leaf depth of a nondeterministic protocol accepting exactly the 1-inputs. The superscript records the accepted side; it is unrelated to their n_1(f), which imposes one witness per input.
recommended_map_wording.communication_relationship: If f has at least one 1-input, Proposition 3 gives N^1_S2(f)=ceil(log2 rc_1(M_f)). Separately, for all-zero f we adopt rc_1(M_f)=0 and N^1_S2(f)=0 using the empty cover and a depth-zero constant-reject protocol. Thus the totalized local formula is N^1_S2(f)=ceil(log2(max(1,rc_1(M_f)))).
recommended_map_wording.local_relationship: Under the fixed bipartition, lr_B(A_G)=lbc(G) because row/column participation is exactly vertex participation. This is different from bounding the number of rectangles covering each 1-cell.
